surprises.head: Nashville shut down Vegas’s power play
surprises.body: Vegas has one of the league’s most dangerous power plays. Not tonight: 0.0 expected goals per 60 on the power play, against their usual 8.9 and a league average of 7.6. A team strays this far about once every 450 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

surprises.head: A rough night for Juuse Saros
surprises.body: Saros allowed 5 goals on 25 shots, worth 2.2 expected goals: 2.8 more than expected. Starting goalies have a night this rough about once every 25 starts.

story.head: The Golden Knights beat the Predators
paras: Ryan O'Reilly struck first for the Predators early in the first, but Tomáš Hertl tied it up for Vegas just under three minutes later. Jack Eichel put the Golden Knights up 2-1 later in the period. Adin Hill stopped Jack Drury on a penalty shot midway through the first. Adam Edström tied it 2-2 for Nashville shorthanded midway through the second, but that’s where Nashville’s luck ran out. William Karlsson put the Golden Knights up 3-2 late in the period. Trevor Connelly and Brett Howden scored a minute and a half apart early in the third to make it 5-2, and the Predators had no answer.
The chances were closer than the score. Juuse Saros allowed five goals on 25 shots for the Predators. The Golden Knights moved to 6-2-0, and the Preds fell to 2-2-2.
